conclusion: The first untuned paired run failed exact-ASR reproducibility despite equal PCM and low lag. Fixed input blocks pass both reversed-order pairs; all four post-change arms have identical PCM and normalized ASR units. Each loaded arm translates six segments live and advances minutes through segment four of six. The last two segments remain pending at stop; no after-timing catch-up is claimed.
limitations: Paced ffmpeg Engine replay, not physical microphone or a natural/long meeting.
Small synthetic language switch from pinned public read-speech; MER around 30% remains a smoke baseline, not good product accuracy. No name/speaker quality claim.

Fixed blocks trade extra buffering for deterministic leveling/decoding: post-change live p95 lag 424–429ms versus old 320–348ms. Single-machine descriptive observations, not a controlled optimization speedup.
Raw telemetry starts after start_capture; negative final capture-wall overhead reflects that origin and capture packetization, not a faster-than-real-time recording or clock/drop guarantee.
Metal worker events and final-worker offload logs bind real GPU use; no energy/GPU physical-allocation/PSS figures were measured. Sampled process-tree RSS can double-count shared pages.
M1–M4, real device reset/OOM, microphone capture, long meetings and semantic translation/minutes quality still need acceptance.
